# Skills Reference — 42 Slash Commands

Skills are slash commands that inject a focused prompt into your Claude Code session — no subagent, instant output.

Install them with `./install.sh`, or copy them yourself:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/commands
cp FoundryAI/skills/*.md ~/.claude/commands/
```

---

## Code Quality

### `/review`
Thorough code review covering logic, security, performance, and readability

```
/review <File path or paste code to review (leave blank to review current file)>
```

### `/review-ai`
AI-specific code review — prompt injection, hallucination risks, token waste, eval gaps

```
/review-ai <File path, prompt text, or AI feature description to review>
```

### `/refactor`
Structured refactoring — improve code quality without changing behavior, with a safety checklist

```
/refactor <Paste code or describe what to refactor>
```

### `/debug`
Structured debugging — reproduce, isolate, hypothesize, fix

```
/debug <Describe the bug or paste the error message>
```

### `/security-scan`
Quick security scan of the current file or code — OWASP top 10, common vulnerabilities, fast triage

```
/security-scan <Paste code to scan or leave blank for current file>
```

### `/test-plan`
Generate a complete test plan — unit, integration, E2E, edge cases, and coverage targets

```
/test-plan <Describe the function, feature, or system to test>
```

### `/explain`
Explain any code, system, or concept in plain language — with analogies, diagrams, and examples

```
/explain <Paste code or describe what you want explained (leave blank to explain current file)>
```

## Feature Development

### `/feature`
Kick off a new feature — auto-routes to the right agents for requirements, design, and implementation

```
/feature <Describe the feature you want to build>
```

### `/architect`
Route architecture decisions to the right specialist — AI systems, cloud, data, integration, security, application, or cross-team

```
/architect <Describe the architecture decision or design challenge>
```

### `/design`
Route any design, UX, or product experience task to the right specialist — research, UX, visual design, or content

```
/design <Describe the design challenge or experience you want to create>
```

### `/prd`
Write a lean PRD — user stories, acceptance criteria, scope boundaries, success metrics

```
/prd <Describe the feature or product idea>
```

### `/spec`
Write a technical spec for a component, system, or API — interface, behavior, error cases, constraints

```
/spec <Name and describe the component or system to spec>
```

### `/estimate`
Estimate a task — complexity sizing, breakdown, risks, and unknowns

```
/estimate <Describe the task or feature to estimate>
```

## AI / LLM Specific

### `/prompt`
Optimize any prompt — improve clarity, reduce tokens, add structure, test edge cases

```
/prompt <Paste the prompt you want to optimize>
```

### `/eval`
Design an eval suite for any LLM feature — metrics, test cases, pass/fail criteria, regression strategy

```
/eval <Describe the LLM feature, prompt, or agent behavior to evaluate>
```

### `/rag-design`
Design a RAG system — chunking strategy, embedding model, vector DB selection, retrieval approach

```
/rag-design <Describe your use case, document types, and scale requirements>
```

### `/cost-check`
Estimate LLM token cost for a feature, prompt, or workflow — with optimization recommendations

```
/cost-check <Paste a prompt, describe a feature, or share your current usage numbers>
```

### `/agent-design`
Design a new Claude Code agent — generates the full agent file ready to drop into ~/.claude/agents/

```
/agent-design <Describe the specialist you want to create (role, domain, what they're best at)>
```

### `/agent-systems`
Design multi-agent systems — orchestration patterns, tool use, memory, planning loops, failure handling, evaluation

```
/agent-systems <Describe the autonomous agent system or agentic workflow to design or improve>
```

### `/mlops`
Design ML training pipelines, model serving infrastructure, fine-tuning workflows, and production ML monitoring

```
/mlops <Describe the ML system, model, or infrastructure you're building or improving>
```

### `/responsible-ai`
Audit AI systems for bias, fairness, safety, and explainability — with actionable remediation

```
/responsible-ai <Describe the AI system, model, or feature to audit>
```

### `/experiment`
Design experiments — A/B tests, statistical analysis, ML model evaluation, research benchmarking

```
/experiment <Describe the hypothesis, model, or behavior you want to test>
```

## Safety, Compliance & Accessibility

### `/compliance`
Review AI/data product compliance — GDPR, CCPA, EU AI Act, HIPAA, data privacy, regulatory readiness

```

```

### `/accessibility`
Audit and fix accessibility issues — WCAG 2.2 compliance, screen readers, keyboard navigation, ARIA, color contrast

## Docs & Community

### `/docs`
Write documentation for any function, module, API, or system

```
/docs <Paste code, function name, or describe what needs documenting>
```

### `/changelog`
Generate a CHANGELOG entry from recent git commits

```
/changelog <Version number (e.g. 1.2.0) or leave blank to auto-detect>
```

### `/release`
Draft release notes — what's new, breaking changes, upgrade steps, migration guide

```
/release <Version number and optionally what changed (e.g. "2.0.0 — new auth system")>
```

### `/standup`
Generate a standup update from recent git activity and session context

```
/standup <Optional context — team name, any blockers, or what you're working on today>
```

### `/onboard`
Generate an onboarding guide for a new engineer joining this codebase

```
/onboard <Describe the project, stack, or specific area to onboard into (leave blank for full project)>
```

### `/devrel`
Build a developer relations strategy — community, DX audit, technical content, OSS, developer portal

```
/devrel <Describe the product, API, or platform and your developer audience>
```

